entries.title: Business days
entries.covers: live table observed spanning Mon 31 Aug 2026 - Mon 1 Jan 2029
entries.notes: The Exchange's own published trading-impact table for its Bank Holidays. States that LSE "recognise[s] the Public and Bank Holidays of England & Wales" and lists, per holiday, whether on-Exchange trading is a NON-trading day or a half day (12:30 close). No standalone yearly PDF calendar was linked from the page at time of retrieval (only a business-parameters spreadsheet and a trading-system guide); the HTML table itself was used instead.

entries.title: UK bank holidays (England and Wales division)
entries.notes: GOV.UK's published list of bank holidays for England and Wales, including the already-shifted ("Substitute day") dates and the one-off Platinum Jubilee (2022-06-03) and State Funeral (2022-09-19) bank holidays and the 2020 VE Day and 2023 Coronation early-May moves. GOV.UK only publishes a rolling window (roughly the current year, several years back and several years forward); it does not go back to 2000.

entries.title: Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971
entries.notes: Statutory basis for the New Year's Day, Easter Monday, early May, Spring and Summer bank holidays and Boxing Day in England & Wales, and for Royal Proclamations appointing additional or moved bank holidays (used for the one-off Jubilee/Royal Wedding/State Funeral days). Good Friday and Christmas Day are common-law holidays, not listed in the Act itself.

entries.title: Pre-Consultation on moving the May Day Bank Holiday (DCMS, May 2011)
entries.publisher: Department for Culture, Media and Sport
entries.notes: Official government consultation document. Section 2.1 tabulates how each regular bank holiday is established in law (Royal Proclamation, the 1971 Act, or common law) for England & Wales. Section 2.3 records that 2011 had "3 bank holidays (4 in 2011 due to the Royal Wedding)" clustered around Easter/May, corroborating that 29 April 2011 was an additional bank holiday.

entries.title: 2012 Diamond Jubilee Extra Bank Holiday: Impact Assessment (DCMS/BIS)
entries.publisher: Department for Culture, Media and Sport
entries.covers: published 2011, covers the 2002 and 2012 Jubilee bank holidays and references the 2011 Royal Wedding
entries.notes: Official government impact assessment. States: "The late May bank holiday will be moved to Monday 4 June 2012 and the extra bank holiday will take place on Tuesday 5 June 2012"; and, discussing precedent, that for the Golden Jubilee "the late May bank holiday was also moved to Monday the 3rd of June 2002 and this was followed by an additional bank holiday on Tuesday the 4th of June 2002." Also references "the Royal Wedding on April 29th 2011" as a comparable national holiday.

entries.title: Trading Calendar 2021 (Turquoise / London Stock Exchange / Borsa Italiana / …)
entries.notes: LSE-published multi-venue trading calendar with one column per venue and a per-venue "Early Closing Time" header row; the London Stock Exchange column's early-closing time is **12:30**. December 2021 rows: Fri 24 Dec 2021 marked Early Close, Mon 27 and Tue 28 Dec 2021 marked Market Closed, Fri 31 Dec 2021 marked Early Close. Confirms both the ordinary 24/31-December half day and the 2021 Christmas/Boxing cascade.

entries.title: Trading Calendar 2022 (Turquoise / London Stock Exchange / Borsa Italiana / …)
entries.notes: Same format. 24 and 31 December 2022 both fell on a Saturday and appear nowhere in the calendar; instead **Fri 23 Dec 2022 and Fri 30 Dec 2022 are marked Early Close in the London Stock Exchange column** (12:30), with Mon 26 and Tue 27 Dec 2022 marked Market Closed. Primary-source confirmation of the preceding-business-day half-day shift.

entries.title: Trading Calendar 2023 (Turquoise / London Stock Exchange / Borsa Italiana / …)
entries.notes: Same format. 24 and 31 December 2023 both fell on a Sunday; **Fri 22 Dec 2023 and Fri 29 Dec 2023 carry the London Stock Exchange early-close marking** (12:30), with Mon 25 and Tue 26 Dec 2023 marked Market Closed. Second primary-source confirmation of the same shift.

entries.title: `exchange_calendars` 4.11, XLON calendar
entries.notes: **Not a primary source and not cited by any event source.** Cross-validation reference only. It agrees with this calendar on all 315 compared rows, including the six pre-2022 preceding-Friday half days that no primary document we located covers (2000, 2005, 2006, 2011, 2016, 2017); that agreement is reported here as corroboration, but those six dates are justified by the LSE's own published shift behaviour (`lse-trading-calendar-2022`, `lse-trading-calendar-2023`, `lse-business-days` 2028), not by the library.

entries.title: Secondary Markets Factsheet, December 2012 (tables T1 Trading Summary and T3 Monthly Order Book Trading)
entries.notes: The exchange's own monthly trading-day counts from October 1997 to December 2012 (table T3) and the 2011-2012 year totals (T1). Every month and year from 2000 equals the modelled count of weekdays less scheduled closures, including the months of every known disruption (April 2000: 18, September 2001: 20, July 2005: 21, November 2007: 22, September 2008: 22, October and November 2009: 22 and 21, February 2011: 20), so each disrupted day counted as a trading day. T3's May and August 2012 rows print raw weekday counts (23); T1's 2012 total of 252 and the May 2012 Monthly Market Report (22 trading days on the LSE, 23 on Turquoise) settle the year at the modelled count.

entries.title: Over 200 million electronic equity trades during 2007 (9 January 2008)
entries.publisher: London Stock Exchange Group (via Borsa Italiana)
entries.notes: States 253 trading days in 2007 and 252 in 2006 (and 19 in December 2007), equal to the modelled counts; corroborates the factsheet T3 months for those years. The December 2008 report (https://www.borsaitaliana.it/borsaitaliana/ufficio-stampa/comunicati-stampa/2009/090109-monthly-report-dicembre-08.en.htm) likewise states "254 trading days on the London Stock Exchange in 2008, one more than during 2007", and the December 2004 report (https://mondovisione.com/news/monthly-market-report-for-december-2004-december-trading-highlights-a-strong-200-2011124/) "254 trading days in the year as a whole, compared with 253 in 2003".

entries.title: Market Announcement, 5 April 2000
entries.publisher: London Stock Exchange (RNS; also republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: The exchange's announcement of the delayed open at 15:45 and the extension of the close to 18:30 on 5 April 2000: a trading day with a late open, not a closure.

entries.title: Service Announcement: Service Update 7 and Service Update 8, 8 September 2008
entries.publisher: London Stock Exchange (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: The connectivity outage of 8 September 2008: reconnection from 14:45, an auction, continuous trading from 16:00 and "we will close as normal at 4.30" (the exchange's spokeswoman as quoted by The Register); September 2008 counts 22 trading days in the exchange's own statistics. A trading day with a seven-hour halt, not a closure.

entries.title: Statement following trading disruption, 26 November 2009
entries.publisher: London Stock Exchange (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: Halt from 10:33 with continuous trading resumed at 14:00 and a normal close; November 2009 counts 21 trading days in the exchange's statistics (9 and 26 November both counted).

entries.title: London Stock Exchange Group cash equity markets resume trading / Resumption of continuous trading, 25 February 2011
entries.publisher: London Stock Exchange Group (republished by Mondo Visione)
entries.notes: Trading paused at 08:03, halted at 08:33 and resumed at 12:15; the exchange "does not intend to extend its scheduled trading hours", so the day closed normally. February 2011 counts 20 trading days in the exchange's statistics.

entries.title: Market Notice N15/22 - Trading Update, 9 September 2022
entries.notes: After the death of Queen Elizabeth II: "all ... markets will open as normal today and will close at the normal times". Negative evidence for the mourning period.

entries.title: Market Notice N16/22 - Trading Update, 12 September 2022
entries.notes: Confirms the closure of 19 September 2022, the bank holiday for the State Funeral: the exchange's own notice for a closure already modelled from the gazetted bank holiday.

entries.title: Service Announcement Notice 001/20102023 - 19 October 2023 - Technical Incident Update
entries.notes: Order-book securities outside the FTSE 100, FTSE 250 and IOB (partition 3) were halted from 15:11 to the close with no closing auction for them; the FTSE 100, FTSE 250 and IOB closed normally. A partial-instrument incident, not a market closure or early termination; no row.

entries.title: Service Announcement Notice 001/05122023 - 05 December 2023 - Technical Incident Update
entries.notes: Two partition-3 halts during the day; the closing auction ran at 16:30 as scheduled. Not a closure; no row.
